title: The Wolf of the Wood
author: Gabriel Mailhot (story), draft 03/10/2026, revised with his rulings (nights of watch, exploration scene)

stages.journal: {giver} has asked you to look into the beast said to haunt the wood by {village}.
stages.canvas: The lord raises it reluctantly, half embarrassed to speak of a beast out of a nurse's tale, half afraid it is true. He wants someone he trusts to go and see, quietly.
facts: Women of {village} have gone missing since the harvest.
The villagers say a werewolf takes them by night.
The lord does not know what to believe and cannot spare his own men to chase tales.

{giver}: Your people at {village} say a werewolf haunts the wood and takes women by night. Three are missing since the harvest.
You do not believe in werewolves, but you cannot explain the missing women either.

stages.journal: Ask the people of {village} what they have seen.
stages.canvas: The villagers are frightened and half ashamed of their fear. They speak of the beast in lowered voices, and each adds a detail of their own.
facts: Three women have vanished since the harvest, each taken at night.
Shepherds heard howling and saw something large moving at the edge of the wood.
Nobody has seen the beast clearly.
The disappearances happen near the old charcoal-burners' track.

locals_of:{village}: You believe a werewolf haunts the wood; someone you know swears she saw its eyes.
Three women have gone missing since the harvest, each taken at night.
It always happens near the old charcoal-burners' track, at the edge of the wood.

stages.journal: Keep watch by the wood of {village} at night.
Something moves in the wood by {village}.

opening.canvas: Another cold night of waiting by the wood. Then the player notices something on the path: quiet, watchful, the dark close around them. End by asking what they do.
facts: Fresh boot prints in the mud lead from the edge of the village into the wood.
The prints are of many men, not of any beast.

findings.text: A trampled clearing with a dropped iron collar and a length of chain.
A wolf pelt rigged on a wooden frame, eyes of polished stone: the beast the shepherds saw.
Cart ruts leading out of the wood toward the road to the coast.

encounters.name: a girl from {village}
encounters.persona: barefoot, shivering, escaped from the slavers' camp two nights ago and hiding in the wood since
knows: Men took her, not a beast; they wore the wolf skin to frighten the village.
They keep the women in a camp deeper in the wood and wait for a buyer from the coast.
encounters.materialize_when: the player offers to take her home to {village}

scene.closing: Whatever the player did, they leave the wood knowing it was men, not a beast, and that the missing women are being sold.

hazards.trigger: pushing through the undergrowth off the track without care
being seen or heard by the slavers' lookout near their camp

stages.journal: Tell {giver} what you found in the wood.
stages.canvas: The lord hears it, and his embarrassment turns to cold anger: men on his own land, selling his people. He gives the order without hesitation.
facts: There is no werewolf: a band of slavers takes the women and sells them.
The lord wants the band found and destroyed.
He will reward the player when it is done.

{giver}: The player has just told you what they found in the wood: boot prints, chains, a wolf pelt on a frame. There is no werewolf; slavers are taking your people to sell them.
You want the band found and destroyed.

stages.journal: Find the slavers near {village} and destroy them.

locals_of:{village}: Word has come that it was men, not a beast. You pray the lord's champion finds them before they take anyone else.

stages.canvas: Relief and gratitude, plainly given. The lord will not forget who unmasked the wolf.
facts: The women of {village} will be safe again.

{giver}: The player has destroyed the slavers who preyed on {village}.

reward.memory: The player unmasked the 'werewolf' of {village}: slavers, whom they destroyed at my word.

consequences.text: A stranger came at the lord's word and ended the wolf of the wood. It was men all along, selling our women.

consequences.summary: The 'werewolf' of {village} was a band of slavers, destroyed at the word of {giver}.

failure.memory: I asked the player to look into the beast of {village}, and nothing came of it.

consequences.text: The lord sent someone about the beast. Nobody came, and the women are still gone.
